done_when: In v1.2.51, when close finds stale guides in Forge’s own checkout, its Next line tells the user to run uv run --frozen forge sync in the affected checkout, and that command regenerates the guides from the branch’s templates.

known.title: Not done: Version-changing source fixes still suggest plain forge sync
Standard: Isolate host-side configuration from tests
Test: Stale source guides in a version-changing fix

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A Forge release fix changes its version pin while a guide is stale. The Done-when item is: “In v1.2.51, when close finds stale guides in Forge’s own checkout, its Next line tells the user to run uv run --frozen forge sync in the affected checkout, and that command regenerates the guides from the branch’s templates.”
The new command is selected only in `check_guides`. When the branch pin differs from the default branch, `src/forge/close.py:825-828` bypasses that function; `close.py:837-847` checks with the running package and still emits the plain `forge sync` instruction from `close.py:62-63`. If that package’s templates differ from the branch, following the instruction writes the installed templates, and close can accept guides that remain stale for the branch.
findings.title: Not done: Version-changing source fixes still suggest plain forge sync

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate - Standard: “Isolate host-side configuration so tests never use or change the developer's settings.”
Case: normal use - A developer runs the suite with `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` set to an absolute path for their Forge environment. This test removes `VIRTUAL_ENV` but inherits that setting, so `uv run` syncs the temporary fixture project into the developer’s environment. It can replace the editable Forge installation with one pointing at the temporary worktree, interfering with concurrent tests and breaking the environment after cleanup. [uv documents that an absolute project environment is reused across projects](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/config/#project-environment-path); the existing clone test selects a test-owned environment at `tests/test_fix_clone_gets_test_tools.py:36-38`.
findings.title: Standard: Isolate host-side configuration from tests

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - A Forge release fix changes its version pin and has a stale guide. The named proof creates the source configuration before branching and changes only the template here, so the branch and default pins remain equal. It never reaches the version-changing path in `src/forge/close.py:825-847`, which still suggests plain `forge sync` and checks against the running package’s templates. The test therefore passes while that part of the Done-when behavior is false; extend the command-level proof to cover a source version change.
findings.title: Test: Stale source guides in a version-changing fix

why: When Forge’s branch templates differ from the installed release, the suggested sync can regenerate guides from the installed templates and leave close blocked.
